illustrations.position_quote: A truncated axis can make visual differences look larger, but it is not automatically invalid; judge whether the scale and labels allow an accurate interpretation.
illustrations.description: Two side-by-side bar charts showing the same pair of values, one with a y-axis starting at 0 and one with a y-axis starting close to the values, with identical bar labels and numbers.
illustrations.why: Seeing the same numerical difference on two axis scales makes the visual exaggeration caused by truncation immediately clear.

illustrations.position_quote: A scatter plot can still contain a nonlinear relationship even when its linear correlation is weak or zero, so inspect the shape instead of assuming that "no linear correlation" means "no relationship of any kind."
illustrations.description: A scatter plot with points following a clear U-shaped curve, showing a strong nonlinear pattern despite little straight-line trend.
illustrations.why: The figure would make the difference between no linear correlation and no relationship visible instead of leaving it as an abstract warning.
